New on HBO Max in December 2026: All the new shows and movies to watch

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Are you ready for a rude reminder about the fragility of time?
  • It has been revealed that things kick off on December 1 with a fist-pumping throwback as an iconic, multi-decade boxing franchise — spanning from Sylvester Stallone’s 1976 classic to its modern spinoffs — steps into the ring.
  • Recent findings suggest that over on the TV side, the platform is capping things off on Christmas Day with a polarizing new series adaptation that kicks off a fresh era for a massive wizarding franchise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Are you ready for a rude reminder about the fragility of time? December is nearly here. Impossibly, we’re already heading into the final stretch of 2026, though at least the best streaming services are helping to soothe that calendar shock with a fresh slate of upcoming movies and TV highlights. And HBO Max, in particular, has a stacked lineup with which to spend your final weeks of the year.

It has been revealed that things kick off on December 1 with a fist-pumping throwback as an iconic, multi-decade boxing franchise — spanning from Sylvester Stallone’s 1976 classic to its modern spinoffs — steps into the ring. Elsewhere on the film front, a provocative comedic thriller led by the winning duo of Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman makes its streaming debut on December 4, before an acclaimed sci-fi horror sequel lands later in the month to keep things spooky.

Recent findings suggest that over on the TV side, the platform is capping things off on Christmas Day with a polarizing new series adaptation that kicks off a fresh era for a massive wizarding franchise. From nostalgic knockouts to broomstick-flying drama, here’s a guide to everything new on HBO Max in December 2026.

Sources indicate that one of the most talked-about new movies of the so-called "awards season" thus far has been "I Play Rocky," an underdog biopic starring Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone during the tumultuous production of his iconic boxing flick "Rocky," which famously went on to win the Oscar for Best Picture. But before you tune into that new bio-drama, why not go back to where it all started with a big "Rocky" movie marathon?

Helpfully, HBO Max isn't just bringing back the 1976 original — which is celebrating its major 50th anniversary this year and centers on a small-time Philadelphia boxer (Stallone) who gets a once-in-a-lifetime chance to face the world heavyweight champion in the ring — but all nine films in the "Rocky" franchise beginning on December 1. That includes the "Rocky" sequels “Rocky II” (1979), “Rocky III” (1982), “Rocky IV” (1985), “Rocky V” (1990) and “Rocky Balboa” (2006), as well as the Michael B. Jordan-led "Creed" spinoff trilogy comprising “Creed” (2015), “Creed II” (2018) and “Creed III” (2023).

That should keep you busy until Latest Year's, right?

Stream "Rocky" on HBO Max starting December 1.

Few Hollywood stars had a 2026 like Olivia Wilde, who directed arguably the year's best comedy, "The Invite," and also pops up opposite Pedro Pascal in the cellist dramedy "Behemoth!" and alongside Cooper Hoffman in this Gregg Araki-directed erotic comedy.

In "I Want Your Sex," Wilde plays renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy, who takes fresh-faced twentysomething Elliot Bell (Hoffman) as her assistant and sexual muse. As their arrangement begins to blur professional and personal lines, Elliot is pulled into a world of sexuality, obsession, power, betrayal and murder.

Along with Wilde and Hoffman, the star-studded cast includes Charli XCX, Mason Gooding, Chase Sui Wonders, Johnny Knoxville, Margaret Cho and Daveed Diggs.

Stream "I Want Your Sex" on HBO Max starting December 4.

It has been revealed that one of the most anticipated TV titles of the year has also been its most controversial, drawing backlash over J.K. Rowling's involvement, casting choices, and, most odd of all, children's teeth. Regardless, plenty of HBO viewers will undoubtedly be tuning into another year at the Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, with a new set of fresh faces playing some of modern-day literature's most iconic characters.

The eight-episode series will follow pretty much the same plotline as the first "Harry Potter" book and subsequent film, with Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, and Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape.

Stream "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" on HBO Max starting December 25.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable.
  • The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do.
  • Sources indicate that it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and people who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

Sources indicate that it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple claims the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

Industry observers note that the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

Industry observers note that if your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

Breaking: Report: Apple job listings detail aims for autonomous AI agents

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of owners.
  • In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.
  • Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of owners. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the company has also introduced fresh restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple confirmed plans to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give users more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

In a recent development, over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted newly introduced job listings that offer a closer look at its intends to develop autonomous AI agents:.

According to recent reports, in one, Apple noted it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

According to recent reports, “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “proposal and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

Recent findings suggest that today’s report on the fresh job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring people to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the organization could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the new job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its prepares for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how promptly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally launched its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A very successful “values-based entertainment” company that was begat — in the parlance of its biblical heritage — from a film-filtering service that illegally edited “objectionable content” out of major Hollywood movies, Angel Studios has since become the world’s foremost purveyor of megachurch-approved multiplex content. The bigger they got (on the strength of projects like “The Chosen” and the QAnon cause célèbre “Sound of Freedom,” the latter of which pioneered a questionable ticketing model that continues today), the more that Angel removed from the films they released. Not just sex and swear words, but also anything that even vaguely resembled a soul. Related Stories Billy Ray Joins Oscar Short Contender ‘Magan’s Fare,’ Starring Barkhad Abdi, as Executive Producer Why Is the ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer So… Gloomy? Internet Erupts Over Latest Look at Marvel Movie.

Industry observers note that with “Hershey,” a decidedly vanilla biopic about the most famous chocolatier who’s ever lived, the studio has taken its socio-religious project to its logical conclusion: They’ve made a movie that’s been stripped of any flavor whatsoever. It’s the cinematic equivalent of carob powder. It’s what Ned Flanders will force his kids to watch next Halloween.

According to recent reports, somehow unimaginatively bland and Splenda-sweet all at once, this godforsaken affront to good storytelling may not have benefited from any of the material that its distributor has deemed amoral, but “Hershey” is so mind-numbingly absent the most basic friction of the human experience that I wanted to fall to my knees and thank the lord that a few errant Kisses made it past The Angel Promise on a technicality. It’s too bad Milton S. Hershey never used his platform to baselessly sow doubt in a foreign election, because at least one of Angel Studios’ co-founders would clearly have been cool with including that (ecocidal fascism is fine, just don’t say “fuck” while you’re razing the Amazon, as that would offend Jesus).

As you may have gathered by now, I am probably not the target audience for this unrepentant godslop.

Not because I’m agnostic (“Hershey” is as secular as Angel Studios’ output gets, its overt religiosity limited to a brief scene in which the movie’s namesake pleads for help from an unspecified higher power), but rather because I stubbornly, blasphemously insist that a womb-to-tomb biopic should bear at least some faint resemblance to the stuff of real life. I couldn’t possibly care less about the facts (though I struggle to believe that Hershey and his wife literally danced with joy after learning that a twist of fate had spared them from being aboard the Titanic), but there isn’t a single moment in this film that feels like it was written by a real person, let alone lived by one.

Let’s back up a beat. To be clear, Angel Studios didn’t technically make this movie — that distinction belongs to the spiritually aligned production company Dandelion Media, who partnered with Hershey Entities for a fully authorized feature-length commercial meant to “bring [the chocolate brand’s] story into culture in a more immersive way.” The success of that marketing spend remains to be seen, but it can’t hurt to highlight Mr. Hershey’s ostensible purity at a time when the company that bears his name has been under fire for diluting its products with compound coatings in order to save money. And so we have a punishingly straightforward film that paints the Pennsylvania icon as a square-jawed, sweet-toothed wife guy who loved candy, orphans, and sitting way too close to the edge of the massive water tower that overlooks the town he remade in his own image.

Directed by Mark Waters, but absent any trace of the poppy confidence he once brought to the likes of “Mean Girls” and “Freaky Friday,” “Hershey” opens with its first and only stylistic flourish as a match cut transforms an immaculate chocolate Kiss into a small lump of coal — Milton Hershey’s life would turn out to be sweet, but it sure didn’t start that way. The film that follows sadly feels less like “Lawrence of Arabia” than it does an AI-generated adaptation of Hershey’s Wikipedia page, its algorithmic sense of human interaction rendered all the more uncanny by its ecclesiastical approach to conflict (and also by its blown out cinematography, which suggests a very literal interpretation of Angel Studios’ promise to produce “movies and shows that amplify light.”).

Adhering to the prosaic structure and candied morality that the Erwin brothers have made endemic to the world of faith-based biopics and their immediate kin, the film sees Hershey’s life as a blessed march towards his eternal reward — one that’s only slowed down by the litany of speed bumps that pop up along his path to heaven.

Recent findings suggest that young Milton’s very serious Mennonite mom is a major bummer, but she lets him out of the house to work for a local printer. The JRPG-like town where he grows up in the 1860s seems inhospitable to dreams, but its muddy roads make it appear as though the streets are paved with chocolate. His dad (Alan Ruck, a long way from “Succession”) abandons him pretty fast, but not before bending down to the kid like Zooey Deschanel in “Almost Famous” and telling him: “You’re a Hershey, and that means when you follow your dream, you don’t let anyone get in your way.” Apparently his dad’s dream was to not live with his family anymore, but so be it. A good example is a good example.

Recent findings suggest that every stumbling block is immediately followed by a burst of divine providence, as Sharon Paul and Timothy Michael Hayes’ script adheres to the grindset mindset of the prosperity gospel while Rolfe Kent’s saccharine score blends everything together into a tasteless slurry of unrefined sugar. The film insists that a little sweetness goes a long way, as an orgasmic taste of rock candy is all that Milton needs to make it through the day, but it doesn’t heed its own advice. Milton’s passion leads him to a job working for a saintly confectioner named Joseph Royer (a beneficent Richard Kind, as close to a live-action Bing Bong as he’s ever been), who just smiles it off when the kid forgets to turn off the peanut roaster and nearly burns down the whole shop.

Recent findings suggest that later, after sprouting into Finn Wittrock and starting his own caramel company, Milton is miraculously spared from ruin several times over by virtue of his non-denominational faith in himself and the universe. One low moment is redeemed by a massive order from overseas. Another resolves with a traveling salesman busting into the Lancaster Caramel Company with an offer to invest in chocolate — the future of snacking! “This chocolate,” Milton sniffs, “it could be good if it wasn’t so bad.” I know the feeling. The next time disaster strikes, he inadvertently stumbles upon the Hershey Kiss in the very next scene. The plotting is schematic enough to make “Bohemian Rhapsody” seem like “Last Days” by comparison.

Somewhere in there Milton enjoys a meet-cute with a woman named Kitty Sweeney (Alexandria Daddario), a grinning beauty who credits caramels with curing her shyness. Her job as Milton’s wife is to be his biggest cheerleader, and then — as the years melt away — to collapse in undiagnosed pain whenever he leaves the room. At one point it is implied that she and Milton have sexual intercourse, but only so the movie can leverage the couple’s inability to conceive a child into a robust philanthropic regime that allowed them to house and educate any number of white male orphans.

Of course, expecting this movie to acknowledge the Milton Hershey School’s history of racial and social discrimination would be as delusional as thinking its third act might address the labor disputes that unsettled Hershey’s chocolate factory in the late 1930s. Such things are simply not sweet enough to befit a story about how some vague belief and a little stick-it-to-em are all a man needs to prosper in this great land — even if a warts-and-all version of that same story would still be a model of American success.

Considerably less textured than the chocolate bars that have become synonymous with its title character, Waters’ film is so determined to launder one man’s dreams into reality that it comes to assume its own kind of dream logic in return — one divorced from the basic relationship between cause-and-effect or an event and its meaning.

In what might be the single most deranged movie scene of the year, Milton and his ailing wife Kitty literally dance for joy on the bow of a ship after learning that a twist of fate has spared them from being aboard the Titanic, even though upwards of 1,400 other people went to a watery grave that night. I’m not sure that qualifies as bringing the brand’s “story into the culture in a more immersive way,” but it’s definitely what I’m going to be thinking about the next time I bite into a milky and delicious Hershey Bar. After watching this perversely chalky film about the manufacturer’s founder, it’s a wonder that I can still remember what their signature product even tastes like.

Angel Studios will release “Hershey” in theaters on Wednesday, November 25.

Breaking: 100 Episodes Of DC's Detective Noir Series Changed Batman Forever

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, few superheroes have a television legacy as rich and varied as Batman.
  • In a recent development, however, one of the best Batman TV series barely features him at all.
  • In a recent development, following Jim Gordon (Ben McKenzie) and the young Bruce Wayne (David Mazouz) immediately after the murder of Bruce’s parents, Gotham styles itself as a detective series that traces the city’s descent into supervillain chaos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, few superheroes have a television legacy as rich and varied as Batman. From the campy action of Batman 1966 to the groundbreaking animated noir of Batman: The Animated Series and the 1940s reinvention of Batman: Caped Crusader, the Dark Knight has flourished on television just as successfully as in theaters. The many Batman TV highlights can feel worlds apart, but each offers an endearing and worthwhile take on the traditional mythos.

In a recent development, however, one of the best Batman TV series barely features him at all. Instead, it takes Batman’s story as the foundation for an ambitious, original crime saga set decades before his emergence, withholding the fully realized Caped Crusader until its final episode. That series is Gotham, and for many longtime fans it’s still considered one of the greatest small-screen Batman stories despite making huge lore changes and completely reinventing the origin of not just Batman himself, but his allies and rogue’s gallery too.

In a recent development, following Jim Gordon (Ben McKenzie) and the young Bruce Wayne (David Mazouz) immediately after the murder of Bruce’s parents, Gotham styles itself as a detective series that traces the city’s descent into supervillain chaos. It turns familiar bombastic supervillains into (initially) grounded characters with their own ambitions and lives beyond fighting Batman. Since its conclusion after five seasons in 2019, few superhero series have managed to make such sweeping changes to a cherished comic-book mythology while still being embraced by devoted fans of the source material.

According to recent reports, making a Batman TV show without Batman in it was always going to be a huge gamble. Gotham makes it work incredibly well, and there’s a key reason why. Rather than ignoring Batman completely for its prequel story about Jim Gordon’s rise through the GCPD, Gotham instead ensures his shadow still looms large by spending 100 episodes creating conditions that make his arrival feel completely necessary by the time he emerges in the finale. The show details Gotham City’s decline from a city plagued by mob rule to a one filled with supervillains that only a costumed hero feels equipped to deal with.

Gotham does this by completely rebuilding the mythology around Batman and the young Bruce Wayne. The network of villains and allies surrounding Batman begins to emerge much earlier than it does in the comic books, and it’s much more interconnected. The villain origins especially change. For example, The Riddler (Cory Michael Smith) begins as a police forensic scientist who works with Jim Gordon and, at one point, is even his romantic rival. Twins Jerome and Jeremiah Valeska (both Cameron Monaghan) play versions of the Joker with connections to Bruce Wayne that mean, unlike the comics, Batman is fully aware of the identity of his greatest foe. Camron Bicandova’s Selina Kyle, the eventual Catwoman, is repositioned to be a childhood frenemy of Bruce’s rather than a thief he meets and falls in love with as Batman.

Giving Batman’s enemies such detailed personal histories is a substantial change to the dynamics audiences expect. It also makes Batman’s arrival feel totally necessary. If there were any chance that the likes of the Joker, Riddler, or Penguin (Robin Lord Taylor) could be redeemed or rehabilitated by traditional means, it would have happened during the years Jim Gordon spent facing them in Gotham. By the time Batman emerges, they’ve become so entrenched in their villainous identities that an equally outlandish figure like the Dark Knight genuinely feels like the only way to keep the city safe from them.

Gotham’s huge transformations also work because they open up storylines that couldn’t happen in the comics, but none of these newly introduced narrative arcs feel like they prevent the Gotham City fans already know from being able to happen. Giving Ed Nygma a sympathetic history doesn’t mean audiences can’t imagine him eventually becoming The Riddler and fighting Batman as an outright villain. Gotham makes substantial changes, but each one feels deliberate and serves the central goal of creating a setting and story that convincingly leads to Bruce Wayne becoming Batman.

Gotham finished its five-season, 100-episode run in April 2019. Its 2014 premiere came before the movie-connected streaming era of Marvel and DC, and before shows like Prime Video’s The Boys and Netflix’s The Umbrella Academy made superhero subversion mainstream. However, despite the fact that superhero media has changed considerably since then, Gotham still holds up. Watching it in 2026 hardly feels like revisiting a bygone era of the genre. The reason why is simple: its appeal was never dependent on being the latest franchise event or cashing in on the superhero boom that began in the late 2000s and early 2010.

The visual identity of Gotham has proved essential for the show’s longevity. It doesn’t feel tied to any specific era, instead having a noir flavor that perfectly fits its unfolding detective story. Old-fashioned cars, imposing architecture, dim police offices, and flashes of modern technology create a city suspended between decades. This production design gives Gotham an atmosphere that can survive changing trends in other superhero media and even in other cop and crime reveals.

In a recent development, its ensemble roster of characters, and the Gotham cast members who play them, are just as key to its legacy. Gotham doesn’t just give Batman characters fresh storylines to pad out time until Batman arrives, it gives them incredibly satisfying narrative arcs in their own right. Gordon’s compromised idealism provides a human center that drives all five seasons, while watching characters like Nygma and Cobblepot trying to turn the pain of their loneliness and social isolation into a meaningful destiny never gets stale. Even Bruce Wayne’s new pre-superhero story feels worthwhile. There’s something incredibly endearing about a Batman who takes up the mantle not just because of the death of his parents, but because of multiple events and encounters with criminals that lead him to decide there’s no alternative to taking up vigilantism.

It has been revealed that the show also grows stranger and more theatrical as it continues, allowing its crime drama to accommodate increasingly grotesque humor and horror as the emergence of Batman draws closer without ever losing its noir detective identity. Most importantly, though, Gotham delivers a complete journey that makes its inevitable endpoint feel earned. The eventual appearance of Batman rewards everything that came before. The ending of Gotham gives its long descent into chaos a purpose, and makes it worth revisiting again and again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Follow our live blog to stay up-to-date on the best sales we find.

Browse our editors’ picks for a curated list of our favorite sales on laptops, fitness tech, appliances, and more.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Industry observers note that not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

In a recent development, when you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be noted for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before fresh models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

According to recent reports, price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

Recent findings suggest that in the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The issue isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

Industry observers note that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a newly introduced tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

It has been revealed that if you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Recent findings suggest that black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Given how often Alan Ritchson has been compared to Arnold Schwarzenegger since he first appeared as Jack Reacher in 2022, there is something rather appropriate about the two being cast alongside one another in a upcoming movie, although the genre they've opted for probably isn't the one most of us would've expected. Ritchson has managed to squeeze quite a few movies in between seasons of Reacher, having worked with Guy Ritchie on The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare and got to mug at the camera with Kevin James in Playdate, but his latest movie will see him back on the streaming service that's helped make him one of Hollywood's most recognizable action stars. And he'll already have quite the audience waiting for him there.

Both Reacher and its spin-off series, Neagley, are officially back among the five and ten most-watched shows on Prime Video in the United States, respectively. According to FlixPatrol's November 23 figures, Reacher sits at No. 5, with Neagley at No. 9, while Amazon's own global streaming figures placed the two shows at No. 4 and No. 9 for the week of November 9–15.

According to recent reports, the success of both shows comes ahead of the December 2 release of The Man with the Bag, which sees Schwarzenegger taking on the role of Santa Claus 30 years after he spent an entire movie desperately trying to get his hands on a Turbo Man action figure in Jingle All the Way. This time around, it's Santa himself who's in need of some help, with Schwarzenegger recruiting Ritchson's thief to recover his stolen sack of Christmas presents.

Alongside Schwarzenegger (The Terminator) as Santa Claus and Ritchson (Reacher) as the thief Vance, the cast includes Awkwafina (Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings) as the elf responsible for Santa's predicament, as well as Berkeley James (Middlehood), Michael Cyril Creighton (Only Murders in the Building), Liza Koshy (The Naked Gun), Kyle Mooney (Saturday Night Live), Jane Krakowski (30 Rock), and Ken Jeong (The Hangover). The movie is directed by Adam Shankman, whose previous work includes Hairspray and Disenchanted, from a screenplay by Allan Rice.

According to recent reports, the Man with the Bag premieres on Prime Video on December 2, while Reacher and Neagley are available to stream now. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest news and updates on the biggest and best movies and reveals heading to your favorite streaming platforms soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 features as much shootin’, stealin’, and drug runnin’ as you’d expect from the latest entry in a series named after a felony. However, some players have been caught off-guard by just how much the early game is all about the more mundane parts of life. Namely, you gotta do a bunch of chores around the house. In many ways, GTA 6 is as much of an everyday life sim as it is a game about committing crimes.

Sources indicate that jason repairs the steps leading up to his and Lucia’s home, fixes a railing, buys groceries, orders flowers, paints the walls of their bedroom, and more to prepare for Lucia’s arrival from prison. All those chores might seem less thrilling than the opening hours you’d expect in a significant-budget action game. But it turns out they set up a tragic heartbreak I simply did not see coming.

[Ed. note: Spoilers for the ending of Chapter 1 follow.].

It has been revealed that chapter 1 involves Jason and Lucia trying to get work from Mattia, the shady boyfriend of Kat, a mother-to-be whom Lucia befriended in prison. Part of that involves a standout sequence set to a Carly Rae Jepsen banger before Lucia gets lost in orgy central. (Vice City, y’all!) Bro, Mattia promises a job that could pay ten grand, bro. They just have to grab a bag from a locker and deliver it, bro.

Industry observers note that red flags abound, but Jason and Lucia go along for the ride, which promptly results in their arrest. Crooked cops show up, the couple gets into a shootout, and Jason gets grievously wounded while the couple struggle to keep hold over a bag containing who knows what.

GTA 6 does a great job of showing how various systems, both governmental and societal, are against Jason and Lucia, and that shines through here. In Jason and Lucia, Mattia sees a pair of not prospective partners, but a down-on-their-luck couple he can easily exploit — and they’re all too willing to play into his hands. Mattia leverages their desperation, even making them play dress up with Lucia in a platinum blonde wig and Jason in one of Mattia’s gaudy shirts, so they’d take the fall for whatever shady shit Mattia is up to. Clearly, he knew the danger surrounding this bag with shady cops and an organized outfit after it and gladly fed Jason and Lucia to the wolves.

In a recent development, they escape, but their horrible night has only just begun. Lucia takes Jason to his friend Cal, who brings Jason — and the mysterious bag — to the hospital. (Lucia later learns the hospital took everything from the couple’s BuckMe checking account as payment. America!) Lucia heads home to recover Jason’s stash, and tragedy strikes.

Upon entering their home, Lucia is jumped by masked criminals searching for that bag. Suddenly, the home Jason and Lucia built is now the arena for Lucia’s fight for her life. Flames engulf the sliding glass door that led to a patio where Jason would work out and the couple would hold one another while sipping their coffee and enjoying the morning sun. Those relaxing mornings are no more.

Tommy’s future crib that Jason bought during his video game night with Cal? Destroyed. A goon even tosses Lucia into it at one point, adding insult to injury. Where Tommy would have slept soundlessly — with a giant stuffed teddy in the corner — is now burning up. Also burning up is the hope that Jason and Lucia will get to live a normal life with Tommy, which the crib represented. Maybe in another life Jason and Lucia would have told Mattia to eat shit, bro, stayed patient, and welcomed Tommy to their little house on stilts in due time. Not in this life, however.

According to recent reports, watching the coffee table get destroyed hurt even more. Building furniture together with a shaky hex key is a quintessential couples activity, and Jason and Lucia do just that during a cute sequence earlier in the game. And then one of the masked men slams Lucia on it, shattering its glass top as their home continues to burn.

Flames raged after I dispatched those enemies. Still, I tried to have Lucia grab the stash from their burning bedroom, only to see her immediately get burned. (She’s fine.) I didn’t want the stash for the money, but the memories.

It has been revealed that in Jason’s metal box, he has polaroid pictures showing him as a baby in his mother’s arms, him in football pads with his best friends, him with Lucia, and him with his army buddies. Jason’s a pretty stoic guy, so I wouldn’t expect him to outright say what these artifacts mean to him, but him keeping them alongside his rainy day fund claims all it needs to. But, just like the crib, coffee table, and everything else, they’re gone. At least I was able to save the photo of Tommy, but not before screaming at my TV thinking I had missed it.

It has been revealed that the house going up in flames is tragic on so many levels. It represented stability for the pair, a stability that they no longer have while trying to survive out of a crappy motel in Chapter 2’s Port Gellhorn. Not only did Jason spend his time fixing it up, but I spent my time fixing it up. I was immediately invested in that home as a result of the work I put into it. Now, it’s a pile of ash.

It has been revealed that everyone whining about the beginning segment of GTA 6 (how dare a game starring a romantic couple have an optional mission for the boyfriend to buy his girlfriend a necklace) missed the forest for the trees. Not only are the activities building a relationship between Jason and Lucia, but between the player and their controllable avatars. I’m over 20% into the story now, and I’ve already come to care for these two knuckleheads in the same way I care for characters in a BioWare game or my Baldur’s Gate 3 companions.

Industry observers note that rockstar’s GTA 6 has taken me by surprise every step of the way with how strong its writing is. I was a bit trepidatious going into it. Could any one game live up to years of massive hype, especially the highest-rated game ever? With its spotlight on two complex lead characters just trying to make it another day in a messed-up world, it’s delivered in spades. At the very least, no other game has made me care about a goddamn coffee table like GTA 6 has.

macOS 27.3 public beta 2 now available, here’s everything newly introduced

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (332 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the firm is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release.
  • Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.
  • Those came alongside several newly introduced features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the firm is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several newly introduced features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

And speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing consumers to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing upcoming tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful revision, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and users on the public beta can now try out these fresh features ahead of their official release.

Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2431 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • [Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “La Bola Negra.”].
  • Industry observers note that with a head of hair, lithe frame, and the soft eyes Caravaggio would’ve loved if the Italian painter were Spanish, pop star Guitarricadelafuente is having a monumental year on- and off-screen.
  • Oscar talk is in the wind, not just for his performance as queer closeted trumpeter Sebastián, who joins the Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War to survive, but for writing the original song “La Nieve.” The sweeping ballad ties together the film’s three story threads that convene around queer Spanish playwright Federico García Lorca’s incomplete text: 1932, 1937 (Sebastián’s storyline), and 2017.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s note: The following interview contains spoilers for “La Bola Negra.”].

Industry observers note that with a head of hair, lithe frame, and the soft eyes Caravaggio would’ve loved if the Italian painter were Spanish, pop star Guitarricadelafuente is having a monumental year on- and off-screen. The gay 29-year-old songwriter finished touring his sensational, sensually charged second album “Spanish Leather” earlier this fall, and only just a few short months after his screen debut, “La Bola Negra,” won a Cannes top prize, got scooped up by Netflix, and entered the awards season fray.

Oscar talk is in the wind, not just for his performance as queer closeted trumpeter Sebastián, who joins the Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War to survive, but for writing the original song “La Nieve.” The sweeping ballad ties together the film’s three story threads that convene around queer Spanish playwright Federico García Lorca’s incomplete text: 1932, 1937 (Sebastián’s storyline), and 2017. Born Álvaro Lafuente Calvo, he’s now a meme thanks to his stage and screen sobriquet, which means “little guitar of the fountain.” Related Stories ‘Hershey’ Review: An Unbelievably Flavorless Biopic About America’s Most Famous Chocolatier John Turturro, Carrie Coon, Guitarricadelafuente, and Peter Gamble to Receive SFFILM Honors.

It has been revealed that guitarricadelafuente’s performance balances both hushed repression and eventually unleashed emotions throughout “La Bola Negra,” as Sebastián nurses wounded (and handsome) Republican soldier Rafael (Miguel Bernardeau, a more established actor in Spain). They fall for each other in the process, in a furtive romance mostly framed in stolen glances and tacit looks — in other words, the sort of good old-fashioned gay yearning that’s made movies like “Brokeback Mountain,” “Call Me by Your Name,” and “God’s Own Country” so popular. “La Bola Negra” is, by now, one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies ever to play in Spain, and it’s a major Oscar contender in select theaters as it gears up for its early December Netflix streaming premiere.

IndieWire spoke to Guitarricadelafuente over Zoom where, behind him, an oversized window frame flanked the waves gently rushing up to Miami Beach. Below, we discuss his songwriting process for “La Nieve,” witnessing the breakup of directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo (which happened during filming), and how he overcame his fears to make his auspicious screen debut. That’s all while balancing a proudly out music career where his sexuality is front and center. Plus, watch an exclusive video about his role in the film at the bottom of this story.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

It has been revealed that indieWire: You’ve been all over the world with “La Bola Negra,” from Cannes in May to Toronto and, now, Miami Beach for this virtual junket interview. You’re used to being all over the place. You also toured your album this year. Did that help you prepare for promoting the film?

Industry observers note that guitarricadelafuente: I would say that kind of, in a way, because there’s something that I see as very similar to going and talking about the movie and talking about your character, which is something very similar to when you’re going around touring with your album. I think it’s more difficult because you need to talk about yourself and not just about playing a character because the music you make comes from a very profound place, and you need to talk about many things that go inside of you.

This is your acting debut, and there’s Oscar chatter for both your performance and the song you wrote for the film, “La Nieve.” Do you watch the Academy Awards in Spain?

Recent findings suggest that not that much recently, but I remember when I was studying architecture in college, I used to stay up late at night doing projects. I remember staying up until 3:00 a.m. and with my friends, we were doing our little houses, and we would put the television on, and see the awards. But that was one of the only times that I stayed up late, or that I used to stay up late to see the awards, because you always receive that in Spain in the morning after.

You signed up for the movie without a script. What was the pitch that the Javis gave you? You knew you’d have to learn the trumpet.

They didn’t tell me that I had to learn an instrument because it was going to be originally something that I already knew how to play, but they wanted to make it more difficult. So they said, “OK, why don’t you try a trumpet?” But yeah, the first pitch, there was not much about it. They told me about “La piedra oscura” by Alberto Conejero, which was the original play where the characters of Rafael and Sebastián appear.

In a recent development, I just knew that it was going to be set against the backdrop of the Spanish Civil War, with Lorca being so present. … They didn’t convince me, but I was so moved by how they were so confident that I could do it because I was so frightened and I wasn’t sure at all, but it was their vision. I admired them so much from before. I knew that they’ve worked with many nonprofessional actors, and people acting for the first time. So it was something that I just threw myself into.

You were frightened about whether or not you could deliver as an actor, or was it the material?

I was spending all of my time making music and touring, and it was very time-consuming and exhausting. … I didn’t know if I could put myself into that experience because I thought the proper way to dig into that role was to put your soul into it.

It has been revealed that they were looking for someone who was openly gay for this role, right? There’s a spectrum of sexualities among the cast. Miguel Bernardeau, your scene partner, is straight.

According to recent reports, well, I don’t even know if we talked about that at any point because it was just assumed that I was. [Laughs] I don’t know if that was a condition. I think it was something that, to be more faithful to the story, had to happen. At the time that they approached me with the role, I was finishing my last album, “Spanish Leather.” It represented an imaginary — but not that imaginary — journey of a young gay man who comes out from his village and puts himself out to the world, discovering who he is and where he belongs.

Recent findings suggest that many people would know my music, but I would realize that not many people knew that I was gay even. There’s a massive, not sexual, but I would say sensual component to [“Spanish Letter”] and this process of growing up and sexual [awakening]. So it was very special in a way to play this role … it’s something that you don’t get that much, maybe in Spain, just to see things where you can get referenced with or reflected with.

In a recent development, los Javis broke up during production. Did they communicate that to the cast? How did you find out?

It was so weird because I don’t know if I’m stupid or what, I didn’t even notice. I would hear obviously so many rumors, but … you couldn’t tell that they were apart because they were acting as one. And I couldn’t believe that they were breaking up with the intensity of that shoot. It was like, “How on earth are they going to split up in the middle of this craziness and this madness?”.

But I don’t even remember when they told us. I think it was at the end of the shoot. We would eventually know that something was going on. I couldn’t believe it. How have you managed to carry this shoot? But that also represented how moving this story was to them.

People were gossiping at that point.

Industry observers note that of course. Even when they reached out to me with the role, I would hear rumors, and I was like, “How is this going to be possible if they’re so tight together?” It was inevitable because they are so well known in Spain, that rumors would arrive.

Sources indicate that miguel has probably 10 years of acting experience that you don’t have. Was he helpful as a mentor, as well as an onscreen romance?

The first time that we met, it was actually when he was doing his audition because the only character that was clear in the movie was Sebastián. We had to test how this approach was going to be with the real Rafael, because this very tight and intimate connection had to happen. He didn’t know that I was going to play Sebastián, and he just appeared in the rehearsal room. And I thought there was a very special instant connection there, that I think we’re obviously very different, or we come from very different backgrounds or different ways of seeing the world.

According to recent reports, but there was a beauty in that because obviously I saw him as this wonderful, beautiful, talented, and professional actor that I could anchor myself in. He’s all the time lying on a bed [on screen]. And so he has to say so many things without being able to move. We were both left a lot of freedom on set and to try and to make errors. The room would get empty, and it was just Los Javis, Miguel, and I.

Were you writing the movie’s theme song, “La Nieve,” during production?

It was a very long process from the beginning, when I was told to write the song. I don’t think of me doing a song as in I get into a room and say, “OK, what I’m going to talk about right now?” And then I get a lyric, and I go back home. This Film has so many stories in it, and to try to be faithful to all of them and try to unify them in a thread, in a song, was very difficult. I was listening at the time, before they reached out to me, to Spanish Civil War songs.

It was actually a queer singer of the time who was called Rolando Alarcón. There were songs played with parlor guitars that were [made] to be sung on the waterfront. We started preparing the role with Los Javis. Lorca had to be very present also in this because he’s all over the place. He’s pretty omnipresent all of the time, surveilling what’s going on. And you had to pay a homage to him because, in the end, “La bola negra” was this unfinished script that he was writing.

According to recent reports, I had to live my character in my own skin and properly carry that emotional baggage that he was holding. And it wasn’t until the end of the shoot, when we were in Cantabria living for two months … I obviously had this melody in my head, but when this scene with the firing squad happens, and [SPOILER ALERT] Rafael dies, it was a combination of all of that emotional journey that the character was living.

I would arrive home that day and start playing a melody on a piano and mumbling some lyrics, and I would send this to Los Javis, and I didn’t know that they were going to use this to unify the three stories that go on in the movie. And it was a way for me to let all of that emotion go.

In a recent development, this song will now have to be part of every setlist you perform. It’s your “My Heart Will Go On.”.

In a recent development, I hope it turns into that. I wish to be 50 years old and be in Madrid and be singing that. That would be so beautiful. Because I feel that I was just playing in Madrid my last concert one month ago, it was kind of the closing chapter of this “Spanish Leather” tour, and the film was just released one week before that. And so I got the chance to play “La Nieve” there for the first time. After that, it was very emotional because you would hear 18,000 people singing to that. It was like goosebumps. After that, people would be commenting on TikTok, “So Sebastián had the chance to finally be a musician and get to Madrid and perform.” That’s kind of like a closing of the thread, a very beautiful thing.

Industry observers note that “La Bola Negra” is also one of the highest-grossing Spanish movies to play in Spain ever. Have you been able to go home and experience that?

In a recent development, we were in Spain those first two weeks until we had the last concert in Madrid, and then we went to Toronto and all over the place. And that was a very special week because I was at my sister’s wedding. You could feel something in the air. There was a communal excitement, and people of all ages, all different ages, going to the cinema, or even people, like aunts of mine, who haven’t been to the cinema in 10 years, to see how that’s happening is something that makes us very proud.

For me, the Spanish premiere was more notable because that’s all Spanish people’s lives. Everybody has been linked to that moment of time, it’s like their ancestors. So the Spanish were going to be the most critical of it. But to see how young people, old people, people from different backgrounds go and you suddenly have this sense of communion was something spectacular that you could see in the streets. Like older ladies and young queer guys coming up to you, it’s just incredible.

It has been revealed that what are you doing next? Do you want to keep acting?

Yeah. It’s been a crazy time. I’m having the time to even make newly introduced music and to, I don’t know, to see what I’m able to, because even three years ago… I would oblige myself to be quiet and rest to be able to feel inspired. But now it’s all these hectic times that are making me feel so inspired, and to share that time and put it into making art.

“La Bola Negra” is now in select theaters will start streaming on Netflix on Wednesday, December 2.

Recent findings suggest that you can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

According to recent reports, as mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

Live now on Steam from developer JackyGames is Auto Chess Souls, a "casual strategy" game that aims to mix the classic roguelike progression system with auto-chess. So far, it's been met with "positive" reviews on Steam, and a lot of that is due to the strategic elements included that elevate it over some other similar games. According to recent reports, that mentioned, note that this is only a limited-time offer, and the promotional period is a bit nebulous. Here's the full rundown:.

"The game is now live and presently free. After finishing the demo, I ran out of money and had to get a job, so I haven’tbeen able to enhancement the game’s content yet. Once it’s complete, it will become a paid game again, but anyone who downloaded it during the free period won’t need to pay. Thank you!".

At this point, Steam developers often need to get creative to sell their game in an increasingly busy marketplace. A lot of games are straight-up provided for free, with no strings attached, in the effort to get the developer's name out there. Others are looking to stand out and get on the "best of free games" list.

With Auto Chess Souls, the studio is taking a decidedly different approach on Steam, telling people to pick up the game now and that, when it's done, it'll be sold to newcomers for a fee. This is pretty much the best of all worlds, as JackyGames will certainly want to make some cash from this to support future development, but you can get in on the ground floor now for free.

Playing Bond does not lend an actor cred with the Academy. But it does extend a career.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monkey D. Luffy has never needed complicated speeches or grand philosophies to make an impression in One Piece. As the captain of the Straw Hat Pirates, he approaches life with an infectious enthusiasm, an unshakable sense of right and wrong, and a determination to follow his dreams regardless of the obstacles ahead. His ambition to become the King of the Pirates drives his journey, but his words reveal that his greatest priorities extend far beyond finding the legendary treasure.

Throughout One Piece, Luffy's most memorable statements offer a glimpse into what makes him such a beloved and iconic anime protagonist. Whether he's challenging powerful enemies, standing up for his friends, or explaining what freedom means to him, his words consistently reflect a remarkably simple yet meaningful outlook on life. Beneath his carefree personality and appetite for adventure is someone whose convictions rarely waver, making his best quotes just as memorable as the battles and friendships that define his journey.

While fans mostly remember Dr. Hiruluk's final words as one of the most iconic quotes from the Drum Island Arc, one excellent quote by Luffy often flies under the radar. During his battle against Wapol, Luffy notably tells Wapol that there are things that are much more vital than power before sending Wapol flying and ending his tyranny over Drum Kingdom. The quote beautifully encapsulates Luffy's values, who, despite wanting to be the Pirate King, a position synonymous with wealth, fame, and power, values dreams and ambition above all else.

Recent findings suggest that though fans have mixed opinions about the first few One Piece films, One Piece: Clockwork Island Adventure has produced one of Luffy's most iconic and inspiring quotes. As Luffy puts it, being able to move forward depends on being able to take risks and this sentiment holds true in every sphere of life.

Sources indicate that luffy's own journey in One Piece embodies this bold spirit. Be it riding up a knock-up stream, breaking into an underwater prison, or challenging thee strongest pirates in the world, Luffy has never been afraid of taking risks and this is precisely why he has made it this far in One Piece.

Luffy's declaration is one of the most iconic catchphrases in anime, a constant announcement that he'll achieve the status as King of the Pirates and find the One Piece. This has been something he's said since the first chapter of One Piece which beautifully lined out his character.

According to recent reports, the first chapter immediately gives fans the reasoning as to why Luffy sets out on his mission to become the Pirate King with his meeting with Shanks and how the Pirate Emperor saved his life. To different people being the Pirate King means different things but for Luffy, he simply wants to be free.

Recent findings suggest that ​​​​One fact about Luffy that has become increasingly clear as the story has progressed is that Luffy will not help someone unless they ask. After all, as Luffy constantly claims, he isn't a hero. While he certainly is kind to a fault, Luffy only helps those who display the resolve to want to save themselves. From Nami at Arlong Park, to Robin at Enies Lobby, and most recently Momonosuke, Luffy has had many such interactions in One Piece which prove he is always willing to lend a hand to those he considers his friends, but only if they truly want to be saved.

It has been revealed that in the conclusion to one of the best fights in One Piece's Wano arc was Luffy's declaration of the kind of world he wanted to make. This scene perfectly captures the type of character Luffy is and how the answers to such serious questions can sometimes come off as somewhat goofy. However, this is a serious answer and reveals just how different Luffy is from most of the other pirates. He doesn't desire to conquer, control, or hold any sort of power over others. He wishes to have complete freedom and peace for his friends and himself to live however they wish.

Luffy's quote on the difference between heroes and pirates puts into perspective how he sees himself as a pirate. While fans will know that he holds to a certain moral code first and foremost he is about himself and his friends. Luffy doesn't want to be a hero, because that means sharing with everyone. If he's going to share, he'd rather keep it to a select few. This is a perfect representation of his journey and why he possesses such a small crew. He doesn't choose the members lightly.

What preceded one of the Straw Hat's most emotional quotes from Nico Robin was Luffy ordering Usopp (guised as Sniper King) to shoot and burn down the World Government flag at Enies Lobby. This scene held incredible significance and showed the lengths Luffy would go to for a crewmate in danger. He was willing to make himself an enemy of the World Government and declare war upon them. Even ready to take on the Marines that came with the Buster Call if it came to it. It's also emblematic of One Piece's counter-cultural appeal, brazenly confronting oppressive leadership, and affirming the notion that no symbol of order is too sacred for pirates if it unjustly takes away their friends.

Chapter 507 was an epic chapter that gave One Piece fans exactly how Luffy would respond if he could find out then and there what the One Piece was. Before Rayleigh could get even a hint of a reply out after Usopp's question, Luffy interrupts.

Industry observers note that luffy doesn't want to know the slightest thing about the One Piece. Not whether it's on the last island or if it's even real. He is far more concerned with the adventure and journey building up to something. Even if it turns out to be something, he will be the one to find out what and he doesn't want any clue as to what it is before then.

Rayleigh tries to gauge just what kind of man Luffy was by asking him if he could control and conquer the seas. But to Luffy, that isn't his goal at all and that being the King of the Pirates simply meant to be the freest man on the sea. Many fans are still trying to wrap their heads around what the One Piece is and what kind of conclusion the series could get. Many believe it will pertain to Luffy's goal and dream to have ultimate freedom. There are many possibilities of what this could be but fans will just have to wait and see for themselves.

According to recent reports, the loss Luffy experienced is still with him, but the initial reactions to the death of his brother are still hard to watch or read. However, Luffy's realization that he still had his crew mates was a huge turning point in the series. From here on out, these are the people that Luffy needs to protect and vice versa. The loss of his brother was terrible, but it also helped him stay closer to those he loved. Ultimately, One Piece is a story about friendship and companionship as much as it's about anything else, making Luffy's declaration that he has friends his best quote.

It has been revealed that created by Eiichiro Oda, One Piece is a multimedia franchise that began as a manga series and follows the adventures of the Straw Hat Pirates as led by Monkey D. Luffy. Luffy, an enthusiastic pirate with a thirst for adventure, is afflicted by a mysterious curse that gives him various powers he uses to protect himself and his friends. The manga eventually gave way to the anime series, with the two being some of history's longest-running anime and manga series. Along with over fifty video games made over the years, the series entered the live-action world with Netflix's 2023 adaptation.

It has been revealed that whatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the fresh limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

Recent findings suggest that whatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the latest limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the upgrade becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company revealed four upcoming features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that mike Plante, a filmmaker and 25-year veteran of the Sundance Institute, died Tuesday after a brief illness. He was 56.

At Sundance, Plante worked as a Shorts Programmer and was a familiar, warm-hearted presence at festival screenings and events.

Industry observers note that “Mike was a treasure to the Institute, the Festival, and our independent film community,” Sundance Festival Director Eugene Hernandez and Director of Programming Kim Yutani stated in a joint statement. “His sense of wonder and humor were matched by boundless enthusiasm and curatorial excellence. Our Festival’s Short Film Program and the Sundance Film Festival Short Film Tour were shaped by Mike’s energy and superb taste in movies. Mike’s roots at Sundance Institute, and his relationships within our organization and festival, run deep. He will be remembered and deeply missed as a true cinephile, a filmmaker, a champion of short films, movie theaters, and film culture.” Related Stories Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination? Guitarricadelafuente Was Terrified to Make His Acting Debut in ‘La Bola Negra’: ‘I Wasn’t Sure at All’.

According to recent reports, in addition to his work at the festival, Plante directed the 2011 feature documentary “Be Like an Ant,” which followed a Vietnam War veteran who builds a house around a mobile home to handle winter living. He also directed numerous shorts including “The Polaroid Job” (2016), which looked at his parents’ work running a paid event-photography studio in the 1980s. It is available to watch on the New York Times’ Op-Doc website.

In a recent development, amy Redford, the daughter of Sundance founder Robert Redford and a board member of the festival, called Plante, “a visionary.” “Through his extraordinary curatorial talent, he rolled out countless storytellers through the vital medium of short film, many of whom have gone on to become some of the world’s most enduring artists,” she said. “Mike embodied the Sundance ethos and played a critical role in preserving the continuity of its values. He was unfailingly generous with his time and mentorship, and a talented creator in his own right. But Mike’s most enduring legacy is his kindness. It was, and remains, the first thing people say about him. His passing is a profound loss not only to the Sundance community, but to all those fortunate enough to have known and loved him. He will be deeply missed.”.

Industry observers note that along with directing, Plante produced feature documentaries by other directors, including “Scrap Vessel” (2009) and “Giuseppe Makes A Movie” (2014). Plante started working for film festivals as a programmer in 1993, eventually joining Sundance in 2001.

In 1998, he started the film zine Cinemad, which he wrote for and produced a podcast. The site championed indie and under-seen movies. Plante also wrote “Sensation Cinema: The Audacious, Defiant History of Louis Sher and the Art Theatre Guild,” which looked at an influential arthouse theater owner and distributor. It was a world that Plante knew intimately. In 2024, he was named head of distribution at The Beverly Theater, an independent cinema in Las Vegas, Nevada. He also worked with the CineVegas Film Festival with Trevor Groth, another Sundance vet, as its Director of Programming.

Plante is survived by his mother, Barb.
