📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that historical dramas remain one of the most popular genres of television and reveals like The Empress prove there are still more stories to tell from European history. Based on the life of the real Empress Elisabeth of Austria (1837-1898), Devrim Lingnau plays 16-year-old Elisabeth as she falls in love with and marries her sister's intended fiancé, Emperor Franz Joseph. Released in 2022, the show was one of the most popular non-English Netflix series of the year and the streaming service immediately ordered a second season and commissioned a companion novel called The Empress: A Novel.

It has been revealed that while seasons on Netflix are not always fast coming, the good news is that there are a lot of highlights like The Empress to keep fans of the show entertained. These shows travel the range from those that are not as historically accurate, as The Empress is not, to those that actually tell historical stories from European history in a way that both entertains and educates the viewers. However, there are also shows that do what The Empress did best, and that is to entertain the viewers with a love story and high intrigue, even if the shows are not based on real events or people at all.

The Serpent Queen, which stars Samantha Morton as Catherine de' Medici, follows the Italian noblewoman as she marries into the French royal family and eventually becomes one of the most powerful women in the monarchy. After arriving at the French court in her teenage years, Catherine navigates complicated dynamics and relationships, dealing with politically charged circumstances as she becomes a royal wife. Following her transformation from outsider to political player, The Serpent Queen echoes shows like The Empress by looking at a woman in a male-dominated royal space and exploring her different way of navigating the intense challenges at hand.

The Empress kicks off its historical drama story with a marriage that is based on love rather than political benefits which is unusual for this world. Interestingly, The White Princess begins with a marriage made purely for political reasons and yet both shows end up telling a similar tale. Jodie Comer stars in The White Princess as Elizabeth of York who married Henry VII in order to end the War of the Roses. However, their marriage soon becomes one of distrust and plotting.

Like Elisabeth in The Empress, Comer's Elizabeth is someone who wants love but finds themselves thrust into a world that sees her as a pawn. She is also strong and capable, refusing to be used, and begins to make moves of her own. It is a thrill seeing her manipulate the king, build her own allegiances, and prove herself a brilliant strategist when everyone else underestimates her.

There is something intriguing about going on a journey with a character who is being brought into such a powerful and prestigious sphere as the royal palace. Elisabeth was an unexpected choice to marry Emperor Franz Joseph and the audience gets to join her in the excitement of seeing where the journey takes her. In Victoria, the protagonist is not as surprised to come into such a power position as she was the next in the line of success, but what Queen Victoria makes sense of her fresh station is similarly a thrill.

Jenna Coleman gives a charming and layered performance as the young queen who inherits the throne and rapidly sets about proving herself. It is another story with love and romance in the royal world, but these aspects are downplayed compared to The Empress. However, both highlights deliver the gripping intrigue of those scheming behind the protagonist's back and these powerful female leads proving themselves as powerful leaders.

Starring Emilia Schüle, 2022's Marie Antoinette follows the life of the titular Austrian princess who becomes the Queen of France after marrying Louis XVI. While her arrival at Versailles as a teenager saw her surrounded by unfamiliar people and traditions, Marie's adjustment to her new responsibilities take a toll on her life as the political aspects of the country hold her responsible for the monarchy's larger concerns. Like The Empress, Marie Antoinette follows a young woman as she enters a foreign royal household and faces the tension of her own personal freedom versus the royal duty she must take on.

Based on the unfinished work of Edith Wharton, The Buccaneers follows a group of wealthy American young women in the 1870s as they travel to England in order to find aristocratic husbands. Their arrival disrupts the traditions of English society, and as they move through their time in the country, they struggle to align their values with the expectations of their fresh surroundings. While The Buccaneers doesn't focus on a royal family, the Apple TV series focus on women navigating the restrictions of European society in a specific time period is reminiscent of The Empress, sharing themes of independence and romance.

According to recent reports, part of the franchise that began with The White Princess, The Spanish Princess carries on the story based on the novels by Philippa Gregory. The historical drama follows Catherine of Aragon, the Spanish princess who became the first wife of King Henry VIII. The limited series mixes historical facts with fiction and dramatization, similar to The Empress. The series covers a large chunk of time until the end of Catherine’s marriage to Henry VIII.

In a recent development, just as The Empress kicks off with a controversial marriage, The Spanish Princess explores the fallout and complications that come from the union. The show celebrates the strength of Catherine of Aragon, as she earns the King’s love and respect. The Spanish Princess excels in the many moments it captures morality and royal legacy, with Catherine playing the same role as Elisabeth, both young women learning how to navigate the throne as outsiders.

In a recent development, four women accept positions as switchboard operators in 1920s Madrid in Cable Girls which makes for a slightly more modern period drama. Each woman tries to gain her independence for various reasons in the male-dominated society, highlighting the restrictions placed on women. The characters are captivating, showing raw emotion whether watched in Spanish or dubbed in English.

Industry observers note that like The Empress, it tells the story of women fighting for what they want in life. In this case, the stories are beautifully written whether about supporting family, escaping high society, or starting a fresh life. However, unlike a lot of typical period dramas, Cable Girls is not as concerned with exploring the romantic side of the story and it's more about these women fighting for their own rights and being at the center of their own story.

Set in Regency-era England, Bridgerton follows the family of the same name as they navigate London's marriage market, where each social season brings new romances, rivalries, scandals, and carefully arranged matches.

Not all reveals like The Empress have to be about nobility and Royal Families. There are also those period pieces that are just about romance and finding love. As one of Netflix’s most popular series, the characters of Bridgerton captivate audiences by following the Bridgerton family during the marriage season. The series follows a different main character with each season.

Sources indicate that fans fell in love with Daphne and the Duke’s passionate love story in season 1, and Anthony and Kate’s intense attraction in season 2. Season 3 offered a new romance to obsess over with Colin and Penelope's relationship becoming the focal point of the story, and season 4 took on Benedict's love story with Sophie Baek. With eight novels in the series by Julia Quinn, there is more love and romance to come. However, like The Empress, it is also interested in using the conventions of this time period to comment on modern society and certain struggles that endure.

Recent findings suggest that the Crown is a Netflix Historical Drama created by Peter Morgan and starring Claire Foy, Olivia Colman, and Imelda Staunton. The series follows the life of ruler Queen Elizabeth II, outlining different points in her life.

Netflix delivered one of the most successful historical dramas with The Crown, following the life of Queen Elizabeth II from her wedding to Philip, the Duke of Edinburgh, to the 21st century. Considering the subject is more recent, the series does an amazing job of capturing the period with elaborate sets and well-written characters to mirror real-life historical figures. The show took audiences through various moments in history and key figures, with three actors playing the Queen over The Crown's six seasons.

It has been revealed that as with The Empress, the series isn’t always historically accurate, with minor details added for exceptional storytelling. The Crown offers a glimpse into the historical significance of the reign of Queen Elizabeth II, while The Empress focuses on a lesser-known tale yet still explores the impact of the real-life figures at the center of its story.

Sources indicate that set in the early 20th century, Downton Abbey follows the lives of the aristocratic Crawley family and their servants in the fictional Yorkshire estate. The series explores themes of social change, romance, and intrigue against the backdrop of historical events, including the sinking of the Titanic, World War I, and the rise of the working class.

Sources indicate that set in the early 20th century, the lives of the Crawley family and their domestic servants are on full display in Downton Abbey. Historical events, like the sinking of the Titanic and the Spanish flu, lend significance to the storylines as the British social hierarchy begins to change. Like The Empress, this indicated the entry into the high class and also featured strong women dealing with class, culture, and politics.

It is also a witty historical drama with an all-star cast, including Maggie Smith and Hugh Bonneville. It’s an addicting soap opera wrapped in beautiful costumes, a lush setting, and perfect pacing. Both highlights enjoyed exploring the unexpected and sometimes scandalous relationships that would emerge in these affluent circles. The show's popularity remains years later thanks to two movies with a final Downton Abbey movie recently announced.

#109247. Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4671 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Indiewire ↗ Open Full Page

Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves.
  • It has been revealed that 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition.
  • “COVID allowed people to acknowledge their inner recluse,” Tim League, the co-founder and former CEO of Alamo Drafthouse, told IndieWire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves. The 1948 Paramount Decrees (named after the studio that pioneered the vertical integration) required studios to give up one of the three options. They decided to give up exhibition. The choice was easy: With low margins on ticket sales and the need to constantly bring audiences in, who wanted to run a movie theater?

It has been revealed that 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition. The rise of streaming was remarked to bring about the end of theaters as we know them. But the COVID-19 pandemic brought exhibition to its closest brink of extinction yet. Related Stories Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56 Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination?

“COVID allowed people to acknowledge their inner recluse,” Tim League, the co-founder and former CEO of Alamo Drafthouse, told IndieWire.

Industry observers note that after the global pandemic, lockdown protocols forced movie theaters to close for months. The luxury theater chain Arclight shuttered all its locations within weeks. Locations closed at a variety of companies, including Alamo Drafthouse. Some theaters survived off of private rentals. Even as theaters slowly reopened, COVID protocols required leaving some seats empty, meaning not all tickets could be sold.

Industry observers note that “I think there was no right move,” League added. “We laid most of our people off. We spent a lot of energy trying to build up a TVOD streaming platform which didn’t entirely work for a lot of reasons… And so we went through bankruptcy, and it was rough. We just ran out of money.”.

“There really was no strategy,” noted Greg Laemmle, owner of the California-based independent theater chain Laemmle Theatres. Since Los Angeles did not allow private rentals, the organization stayed afloat via concessions, pop-up events, and some virtual cinema opportunities. “It was all just trying to understand how we can maintain contact.”.

Exhibition became such an unappetizing business that many of those who jumped on board the irony-fueled GameStop stock inflation of 2021 also bought shares of AMC Theatres, bringing the company to an all-time high in valuation.

Sources indicate that but years later, the theater market is experiencing a rebirth. Driven by new theater operators and new kinds of theatrical experiences, the contemporary exhibition landscape looks very different from 10 years ago.

In a recent development, theater operators paint a picture of an industry that is no longer weathering a storm. Instead, they reveal the trends driving theaters to thrive and the complications with the model that won’t seem to die.

The first high-profile artist-led theater acquisition was Quentin Tarantino’s purchase of the Latest Beverly Cinema in Los Angeles. The director had previously helped fund his childhood theater to keep it afloat before buying the cinema outright and taking over as programmer in 2014. The purchase of the 300-seat New Beverly was partly fueled by Tarantino’s desire to preserve what the digital era sought to make extinct: celluloid projection. Since the director’s acquisition, the theater proudly boasts that it screens only on film, usually 35mm.

Tarantino declined to comment on this story.

In a recent development, A few years later, COVID-19 brought a newly introduced threat to movie theaters. A similar mission-driven attitude took hold in a new crop of directors and artists: to protect not just how movies are screened, but to ensure audiences can still see them in communal spaces.

Industry observers note that independent film director Kevin Smith bought his hometown theater in Atlantic Highlands, New Jersey, in 2024. The Atlantic Twin Cinema was a five-screen multiplex Smith grew up going to, housed in a building over 100 years old. But over time, nearby multiplexes threatened to drive the theater out of business. When Smith’s friend Ernie O’Donnell told him the theater would be torn down to build condos, he resolved to help save it.

Industry observers note that “Anything I ever learned about myself I never learned in a classroom, and I certainly didn’t learn it sitting in a church,” Smith told IndieWire. “But mostly everything I know about myself I learned sitting in the darkness of that theater, looking up at the great white mirror and seeing life reflected back at me.”.

It has been revealed that smith invested $450,000 and partnered with several friends to buy the theater, rebranding it as Smodcastle Cinemas. While he mostly lives in Los Angeles, Smith travels to Jersey every month to work on the theater.

Smith described how the finances of owning a theater in a small town may not always reflect larger box office trends. “Avatar: The Way of Water” opened in 2024 and eventually grossed over $2 billion, making it one of the most successful films in history. But at Smodcastle Cinemas, they only sold 12 tickets opening weekend.

Recent findings suggest that at Smodcastle, the theater has leaned into what Smith calls “The business of Kevin Smith.” This includes Q&As of his films featuring Smith and his collaborators like Justin Long for a “Tusk” screening, and Tracy Morgan for the 15th anniversary of “Cop Out.” The theater started a film festival to help showcase local Fresh Jersey cinema. Smith was working on selling a reality show about the theater’s day-to-day operations, similar to the seven-season run of “Comic Book Men” filmed inside the comic shop he owns, but noted progress has stalled.

“I love calling up Ernie and being like, ‘How many seats [have we sold] so far?’ And he’ll be like ‘120 out of 230,’ and I’m like, ‘All right man, I gotta put 90 more asses in seats. Let me see if I can jump on a radio show… go over to Manhattan and jump on “Good Day Latest York” and try to get the word out,’” Smith explained. “It’s fun, but it is definitely fucking work. I have a feeling Quentin don’t work nearly as fucking hard at his theater.”.

In a recent development, smith elaborated on the work it takes to keep the theater running, “We all got together and saved the theater, man. But it was the worst financial fucking decision I ever made,” Smith said. “Owning a movie theater in the 21st-century post-COVID [world], it’s a dicey proposition at best… We became a nonprofit theater because the movie theater’s never going into fucking profit.”.

The nonprofit model has become an increasingly popular option for keeping theaters alive. In 2012, Los Angeles video rental store Vidiots transitioned to a nonprofit to stay afloat, recasting its mission around film preservation, protection, and education. The organization later received heavy support from Megan Ellison’s Annapurna Pictures, which kept the company running for two years after it shuttered its store in 2017.

Sources indicate that “If you go across the country, you’re seeing a real boom in nonprofit or community-supported movie theaters,” said Laemmle. He highlighted the Tasveer Film Center in Seattle, which reopened the former Ark Lodge Cinemas in 2025 due to support from a local nonprofit that had run a South Asian film festival.

“Why not form a community organization that augments ticket sales with other sources of revenue, or that can take advantage of their not-for-profit status and do the enhanced kind of programming that you can’t do at a for-profit business?” mentioned Laemmle.

The high costs of running a movie theater are also evident in one of the latest major theater purchases by an artist. Director Jason Reitman led a group of 30 filmmakers — including Christopher Nolan, Guillermo del Toro, Steven Spielberg, and Chloé Zhao — to purchase the historic Village Theater in Westwood, Los Angeles, in 2024. Since rebranding as Directors Village, the theater has partnered with the film nonprofit American Cinematheque, which will handle its programming.

Sources indicate that the $12 million acquisition in 2024 rescued the historic theater after its lease with its former owner expired. The filmmakers will pour an additional $25 million into renovating the theater, which was open for programming in summer 2026 but closed in October and will reopen in 2027. The project required an alleged six-figure minimum buy-in from the artists involved.

In a recent development, jason Reitman declined to comment through a representative, citing that it is too early to discuss plans for the theater’s renovation. American Cinematheque did not respond to requests for comment.

In a recent development, jason Reitman and Co. also looked into purchasing the adjacent Bruin Theater but were ultimately deterred by the extensive cost of renovations, as previously reported by IndieWire.

The list of artists owning theaters is only growing. Kristen Stewart purchased the historic Highland Theatre in Los Angeles in February 2026 and prepares to restore the space into a hub for the L.A. film community. Tarantino bought a second LA theater, the Vista, in 2021. Martin Scorsese, Ethan Hawke, and Frances McDormand joined the advisory board of the Upper West Side Cinema Center to turn the former Metro Theater on Broadway in Fresh York City into a five-screen arthouse theater, funded by New York City grants and donors like the Kate Capshaw and Steven Spielberg Hearthland Foundation.

According to recent reports, the trend highlights a fresh form of altruism by creatives seeking to keep theaters alive. But even if the business isn’t financially valuable, there is an argument for artists to be seen as patrons of their craft. “As more and more movie theaters start closing down, every filmmaker is from somewhere, and every filmmaker has their hometown theater,” said Smith. “And if you have a degree of success where you’ve got some side hustle loot and whatnot, what a great way to spend your money.”.

Recent findings suggest that in 2019, the Department of Justice marked the Paramount Decrees for termination, citing changes in the studio system structure and film market that rendered the law obsolete. In August 2020, while most theaters in the United States were shuttered, the Department of Justice ended the decree.

In November 2019, Netflix unveiled it would lease Upcoming York City’s historic Paris Theater, three months after a notice of closure was posted. In May 2020, the streamer bought the closed Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood to be co-programmed between the studio and its previous operator, American Cinematheque. In October 2021, Netflix also announced it would take over the lease of the Bay Theater in the Pacific Palisades.

In a recent development, these acquisitions had a touch of irony considering Netflix made a name for itself by rejecting theatrical exhibition. The streamer did not abide by the then-standard 90-day exhibition window before making its films available on the service. The Academy Awards require week-long theatrical runs to make films eligible for awards. Major chains like AMC Theatres and Regal Cinemas refused to show Netflix films (and still do on occasion; Regal and Cinemark recently unveiled they will not screen “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” due to the shortened theatrical window). But just as it became legal for Netflix to enter the theater market, it did. By becoming an exhibitor, it no longer needed major theaters to show its films.

“Netflix needs screens in the L.A. and Newly introduced York market,” said James Huntsman, the co-founder of distribution company Blue Fox Entertainment Group, which purchased two former iPic theaters in June 2026. “I don’t care if you are Netflix, it’s really hard to get a screen in both of those two markets… So if you’re Netflix and you have six movies that are coming out between October and December and they all need qualifying runs of seven days, full runs in both markets, now you start seeing why they’re interested in screens.”.

Recent findings suggest that amazon Studios opened The Culver Theater — the former Culver City Arclight location, which shuttered in March 2020 after the tech giant went bankrupt due to closures from the COVID-19 pandemic — in December 2022. The theater screens a mix of newly introduced releases, repertory screenings, and hosts premieres for Amazon MGM Studios’ television shows and movies.

In October 2026, Paramount Pictures announced it took over the lease for the Bay Theater, which has been closed since the 2025 Palisades fires. The fresh theater, opened in November 2026 and operated by The Lot, similarly offers first-run theatrical releases from all studios, along with dine-in food.

In a recent development, “We’ll see if it really develops into anything more than just a novelty for them,” said Laemmle about studios purchasing individual theaters. “[They’re] one-offs and just being able to want to say that they’ve got something. But I don’t sense there’s going to be a more prolonged investment, but if it happens, it’d be great.”.

The most high-profile studio entrance into the movie theater market was Sony Pictures Entertainment’s acquisition of theater chain Alamo Drafthouse in 2024. Founded by Karrie and Tim League in 1997, the organization made its name as an offbeat theater option with dine-in service and strict rules against talking and phone use in its theaters.

“I think we came to it from people who loved movies but didn’t really love our options with chain theaters that we had around,” said Tim League. “We were always looking at how we can build this and build a community around sharing movies we love.”.

Alamo Drafthouse began talks with Sony Pictures Entertainment in late 2023 before completing the sale in 2024.

“It was kind of essential to find a newly introduced partner as soon as we ran out of money,” noted League, who has since stepped back from daily operations at the organization and remains involved as Strategic Advisor.

“Why it was appealing for us as a tech giant with our board prior to deciding that Sony was the right acquirer for us is partly because of what that also meant in terms of resources that Sony could offer… Not only in terms of Sony [being] a very substantial, well-capitalized company but reputationally, very financially stable, [and] very well respected in the space,” noted Michael Kustermann, CEO of Alamo Drafthouse and head of Sony Pictures Experiences.

According to recent reports, sony is not involved with day-to-day operations of Alamo Drafthouse. But the parent company’s ownership is evident in occasional special programming, such as airing the Season 4 finale of “Breaking Bad,” which Sony’s TV division produced, in Alamo theaters in September 2026 to celebrate protagonist Walter White’s birthday.

But the largest initiative made possible by Sony’s ownership was the July 2026 announcement that Alamo Drafthouse would purchase the historic Cinerama Dome theater in Hollywood and the attached 14-screen multiplex.

Industry observers note that “This has been the white whale for Alamo for a long time,” remarked Kustermann. He explained Alamo was interested in the location before the Sony deal but didn’t have the financial means to acquire a newly introduced flagship location. But after a couple of years of interest and conversations that did not progress, Alamo reached back out after the Sony deal and began serious talks in 2025.

It has been revealed that the company looks to operate the Cinerama Dome screen unlike traditional Alamo theaters. Dine-in service will not be offered. Kustermann noted that the renovations will be minimal, aiming to keep a similar seat count. The iconic curved screen that defined Cinerama projection will remain, and reprints of films screened in Cinerama such as “It’s a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World” will be part of the programming slate.

Renovations to the multiplex will include adding one or two 70mm projectors, karaoke rooms, an updated bar, and an aesthetic redesign inspired by the theater’s 1960s decor.

Recent findings suggest that blue Fox Entertainment was founded in 2015. The North American distribution and film sales tech giant distributes over a dozen films a year across a variety of genres.“Exhibition is where all the glamour is, right?” stated Huntsman. “Distribution is very labor-intensive; you’re supplying content to a theater, to a platform, to DVD. It’s very back office, administrative.”.

According to recent reports, “I only got into distribution as a way to get into exhibition,” Huntsman explained, adding that Blue Fox Entertainment bought its two theaters to combine the company’s passion for film and enter a new market. “I make no qualms. I’m in the money business, but I’m using movie theaters and film distribution and film sales to do that.”.

When the dine-in theater chain iPic went bankrupt in 2026, Blue Fox bid on six of the 12 available locations and ultimately purchased the Westwood, Los Angeles, and New York City theaters. The dine-in service was removed, but each location has a full-service restaurant attached that does not require a cinema ticket.

It has been revealed that by rebranding as The Cinemas, Huntsman aims to turn the theaters into viable assets that can make money beyond box office revenue. “I have private events, I have two restaurants at these locations, I do advertisements around the exterior. So if you put all that together, it’s not a bad business. If it was just a standalone straight movie theater, it’s a tough market.”.

Recent findings suggest that the economics of why so many newly introduced independent theaters are popping up can be traced to a basic reality of the business, according to Laemmle: the simplicity in bringing a theater back to life. “You don’t need to pay anything to acquire inventory. It’s not like opening a bodega where you’ve got to fill it with stuff. You get a film, you promise to pay a percentage of the box office to the studio, and suddenly you’re in business.”.

Recent findings suggest that ticket split rates can vary per title. The rate can be anywhere from 30% for repertory screenings to over 60% for a blockbuster Disney release. Some studios send a range of split rates that can be negotiated; others (like Disney) set a non-negotiable rate.

A film’s success can also affect how much a theater owner makes per ticket sale. Speaking to this summer’s releases, Huntsman remarked that the underperformance of films like “Supergirl” and “Moana” meant he received a larger portion of the box office. But for major hits like “Toy Story 5,” theaters get a smaller piece of the action.

Industry observers note that studios can also control exhibition through clean policies: the practice that if a theater licenses a certain film, it must be on screen when the theater is open. These policies can be especially detrimental to single-screen theaters in rural areas, effectively limiting the variety of films a community can show.

It has been revealed that at Smodcastle, Smith planned special programming with Vulgathon, a marathon of all the films in his View Askew universe from “Clerks” to “Clerks III” in order. But while ticket sales were tracking to sell out all 900 seats across five screens, Disney said that if the theater did not leave a screen open for the second weekend of “Deadpool and Wolverine,” the studio would not send them the film to screen for its opening weekend.

“So we had to leave one screen open, for fucking ‘Deadpool’ and shit, that did not sell out,” Smith said.

Advertising revenue also dropped dramatically post-COVID, according to Laemmle. He estimates that the company presently makes 25% of its pre-pandemic revenue through theater advertising. “Ad agencies had a budget that they allocated for in-theater advertising in the pre-pandemic world. All of a sudden, movie theaters were closed so they just took those same ad dollars and moved them somewhere else…That was a significant source of contribution to the bottom line that’s really gone.”.

Loss of advertising revenue forces theaters to find fresh revenue streams. For some major chains like AMC and Regal, that includes pay-for-play trailer programming: where studios can pay to put trailers for their upcoming releases in front of new titles. This also incentivizes longer trailer blocks that can run up to 30 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that other major sources of revenue for theaters are concessions, which can offer high margins for cheap snacks like popcorn and pre-packaged candy. Beer and wine sales have also been a major boost of revenue for Laemmle Theatres.

The other option: Lean into alternative programming that may not incur as high ticket splits. The Cinemas has been experimenting with testing various repertory titles across different genres to figure out what titles will draw people back into theaters. Their upcoming lineup for November and December 2026 includes “Boyz in the Hood,” “When Harry Met Sally,” and “The Lord of the Rings” trilogy.

For Huntsman, the need for theaters to diversify revenue reflects the current model for how studios release films. “When I grew up seeing movies in theaters primarily in the ‘80s, there were like three studio releases every week…There was always the rom-com, the horror film, the action film, the indie film…Now it’s ‘Fast and the Furious’ comes out, and nobody releases anything for three weeks.” Huntsman added, “So in terms of profitability, [that’s] part of why we’re making the theater a destination.”.

Rising labor, rent, and electric bills over the last few years have made it harder for theaters to improve their margins. In a search for more profits, theater operators have taken on new initiatives to upgrade the technologies and amenities associated with theater-going to bring in crowds looking for a more premium experience, with varying degrees of success.

It has been revealed that for Alamo Drafthouse, the Sony-owned firm received complaints from longtime fans in 2026 after introducing mobile ordering to its theaters, replacing the original pen-and-paper method that involved more engagement with servers. Instead, guests scan QR codes to place orders that are sent directly to the kitchen.

This move drew ire from the Alamo community, who saw it as hypocritical to the manufacturer’s prominent No Phones policy. The company’s subreddit became flooded with people saying they wouldn’t be returning to the theater amid the changes. Actor Elijah Wood, an Austin local who frequently appeared at events put on by the chain, criticized the latest system, calling it “truly awful” in a post on X.

The company described the QR code ordering system as part of a larger blueprint to ensure long-term stability and keep innovating the experience, citing past changes like introducing reserved seating and ending its adults-only policy.

Recent findings suggest that an Alamo spokesperson said that the organization has not laid off any staff due to introducing QR codes and that it allows servers to handle more tabs. They added the core of the decision was to protect wages and jobs for the company’s staff working 12 months a year, but that QR codes will allow them to hire fewer seasonal staffers.

Tim League declined to comment on the QR code system.

While Alamo Drafthouse pioneered the dine-in model for theaters, League’s newest business venture is to bring exhibition into the luxury space. He launched Metro Private Cinema in 2025, a 20-screen theater in New York City’s Chelsea neighborhood that specializes in small, private theater experiences with fine-dining menus to accompany the films.

Industry observers note that theaters range from four to 20 seats. Bookings start at four hours, and food packages are added to the price. Guests can choose between latest releases, special holiday-themed programming, or a specific movie, plus a la carte food.

It has been revealed that “Since the dawn of cinema, it has been being tightly packed into a large room with a bunch of strangers,” remarked League. “So what if we kind of flip that around, and it’s you’re surrounded by friends. And how does that change the experience?”.

Industry observers note that pricing for the experience can vary. Example packages on the website list costs starting around $200 per person. When asked about introducing a luxury price point into the theater market, League explains that costs align with the high prices commonplace in the city. “Our meals are $115 for a 13-course meal, which is very much in line with Latest York pricing.” League added, “We have built a more higher-end, expensive model, but I think what we’re offering is not ridiculous.”.

Recent findings suggest that if companies are not expanding the price-point of concessions, the other option is to expand the theatrical viewing experience itself. Sony Pictures Entertainment launched Cosm, a 364-seat immersive theater with an 87-foot curved screen, in 2024. Tickets are roughly $50, with some including themed food options. And massive Las Vegas entertainment complex The Sphere received over $400 million in revenue from sales of its multisensory AI-edited run of “The Wizard of Oz.”.

Sources indicate that in recent years, audiences have shown growing interest in premium theater presentations. Major studio blockbusters are expected to have exclusive IMAX runs. Films like “Sinners” and “The Odyssey” have driven a rise in interest in IMAX 70mm screenings, letting audiences see movies in the format directors intended.

Sources indicate that CJ 4DPlex, the developer of premium screening formats ScreenX and 4DX theaters, reported a 26% increase in revenue in the first half of 2026 compared to 2025. Their technology includes 270-degree panoramic presentations or immersive 4DX theaters with moving seats and water effects. Ticket surcharges can range from $3 to $7 for ScreenX showings and up to $10 for 4DX tickets, compared to a traditional 2D ticket.

According to recent reports, but the desire to jump into premium formats is not universal. Laemmle said his theaters have no plans to offer advanced presentations. “We’re not necessarily engaged in the large format with the higher ticket price because we believe that movie-going should be something that’s done regularly…Moviegoing historically was the cheapest form of out-of-home entertainment, and we believe it should stay that way.”.

The movie theater industry has always existed on a wire’s edge. Owners and monopolies have come and gone. Projection trends like Cinerama and Vistavision had their moments before becoming obsolete. Television, VHS, DVDs, and streaming have all carried the threat of being the final innovation that would put theatergoing in the past forever.

According to recent reports, “The death of our industry has been predicted since the ‘50s with every fresh turn,” said League. “I just think there’s [now] pressure not to lose sight of the fragility of being an awesome third space.”.

2026 is currently on track to have the best box office performance globally since 2019, with the year expected to end with $35.7 billion in global ticket sales.

For Huntsman, the increase is corollary to the output the studios offer: that the box office success of “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is more tied to quality than any other metric. “Anyone that says, ‘Oh, movie theaters are back,” they didn’t go anywhere. There just weren’t any good movies playing.”.

At Laemmle Theatres, the biggest draws of the year have been indie success stories, with films like “You Can See Everything,” “NAZA,” and “Filipiñana” bringing the theater some of its largest ticket sales.

Speaking with a variety of theater operators, the common thread in running a successful theater wasn’t what was on the screen. The key was understanding each theater’s audience. For Laemmle Theatres, it’s typically older people who go to the movies often and have a wide variety of tastes. At Metro Cinema, it’s Latest Yorkers with the funds to splurge on an elevated experience for special occasions. And at Smodcastle, it’s Kevin Smith fans looking for programming only Kevin Smith can provide.

The full scale of how COVID-19 changed culture has yet to be fully realized. But the renewed investment in owning and innovating movie theaters speaks to a broader desire to safeguard community spaces where people can exist between work and home. The theater industry’s revenue streams are more diversified than they’ve been in years. The allure of owning a movie theater isn’t just about making money; public goodwill has added intangible rewards for exhibitors for keeping theaters alive.

Or as Smith remarked, “It’s good for the heart, good for the soul, good for the optics, good for the brand.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that fantasy television is a truly intoxicating experience, and in the last five years, fans of the genre have been gifted quite a few gems that are hard to quit watching after the very first episode. From magical adventures and ancient mythology to elaborate fantasy kingdoms and supernatural romances, the genre has continued to keep its fans flushed with exceptional watches over the last half-decade.

Quality standouts like the Disney mythological gem, Percy Jackson and the Olympians, which delivers quite the thrilling adventure, and the intoxicating supernatural fantasy series Interview with the Vampire, which delves into the darker and more emotionally complicated side of the genre, are just two shows that demonstrate just how much the world of magic and otherworldly television has grown and reached upcoming heights. Featured on this list are perfect fantasy shows of the last five years that stand strong as some of the greatest recent achievements of the genre.

Recent findings suggest that this underrated fan favorite unfortunately never got the chance to fully realize its potential due to a rather swift cancellation, but it still makes for a great supernatural fantasy for anyone looking for a great mixture of dark comedy, supernatural mystery, and heartfelt storytelling. Dead Boy Detectives follows two teenage ghosts named Edwin Payne (George Rexstrew) and Charles Rowland (Jayden Revri) who have chosen detective work over moving on to the afterlife.

According to recent reports, dead Boy Detectives' tonal agility is pretty impressive. From episodes that seem like a coming-of-age romance drama, to others that feel like a grotesque supernatural procedural watch, and yet another installment acting out like an absurdist afterlife comedy, the series seamlessly slides between genres without losing any of its charm. With its rather playful, imaginative approach to the supernatural world and a balance of emotional storytelling and fantastical excitement, Dead Boy Detectives remains an exceptional fantasy watch of the last half-decade, even with its disappointingly short run.

Recent findings suggest that my Lady Jane is a historical fantasy drama that is one of the most delightful romances ever brought to TV. Set in an alternate Tudor England, the show centers around the intellectually formidable young noblewoman Jane Grey (Emily Bader), whose family's financial situation, as well as political pressures, forces her into a marriage with a very unexpected man.

Industry observers note that my Lady Jane is host to charming performances, playful storytelling, and a historical setting that makes it a pretty epic watch. The show's cancellation was rather frustrating for audiences, since the series had so much potential to be at least a three-season fantasy standout. Even with its single, brief season and underrated status, My Lady Jane's masterful blend of entertaining enemies-to-lovers romance, period fiction, and magical transformation makes it an unconventional but pretty entertaining fantasy release of its era.

According to recent reports, this 2024 Chinese drama is one of the most visually breathtaking fantasy dramas of recent years. Fangs of Fortune focuses on a powerful demon with an enigmatic relationship to the human world, Zhao Yuanzhou (Hou Minghao), who becomes involved with a group confronting supernatural disturbances after boundaries between creatures and humans begin to destabilize.

This rather dark fairytale-esque show is a pretty solid example of why contemporary fantasy rankings need to look beyond Anglo-American franchises. Fangs of Fortune's visual language is incredibly luxuriant, but its narratively dense story can also feel a bit excessive. Despite this, the series, in the same breath, excels because its density rewards viewers willing to immerse themselves in detailed mythology, richly layered storytelling, and complex characters. Fangs of Fortune is peak fiction, a truly compelling example of contemporary international fantasy television.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians is a pretty good Disney+ series—a recent fantasy adventure that has earned itself quite a devoted mass of fans. The show follows young Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell), who discovers that the strange incidents that have followed him throughout childhood are connected to a truth much larger than his school disciplinary record or any kind of diagnosis.

Sources indicate that percy Jackson and the Olympians truly captures the excitement of discovering an entirely hidden world quite effectively. The series' coming-of-age themes and imaginative adventures definitely make it worthy of the praise it's received since its debut. Percy Jackson and the Olympians, with its engaging central ensemble and colorful interpretation of ancient legends, stands as a worthwhile fantasy gem that makes a great addition to this list of hits in the genre.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

According to recent reports, you want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

It has been revealed that you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

This ambitious work of art is one of the latest fantasy productions of the last five years, and it does a rather great job of immersing audiences in a familiar world of fiction. Set thousands of years before the events of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power centers around Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), who is thoroughly convinced that evil has not vanished from Middle-earth even as many around her are eager to believe the great wars are long over.

In this era of fantasy TV production, no other series has been more visibly burdened by expectation. In response to this, The Rings of Power delivers quite the feast in its languages, civilizations, craft traditions, and historical time. Though there has been a bit of a divide among audiences due to the show's storytelling choices, The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power's dedication to large-scale fantasy and visual achievement makes it quite the major example of how ambitious modern fantasy television has become.

Witch Hat Atelier is an anime fantasy standout that stands strong as one of the most enchanting works in the TV genre. The Japanese series focuses on little Coco (Rena Motomura), who grows up believing magic is a gift possessed only by people born as witches, which makes her fascination with spells a form of longing for a life she thought was never going to be hers.

Through delicate animation, an emotionally engaging coming-of-age story, and carefully developed magical rules, Witch Hat Atelier captures the true wonder that makes fantasy so enchantingly captivating. It's often praised as one of the highest-ranking 2026 fantasy deliveries because of its brilliance. With its peak storytelling and beautiful animation, Witch Hat Atelier earns its place on any list of absolute fantasy standouts of the last five years.

In a recent development, this completely underrated animated masterpiece is an entertaining fantasy series of the last five years simply because it transforms a traditional sword-and-sorcery adventure into a thriller mesh of genuine comedy, absolute chaos, and surprising amounts of emotion. The Legend of Vox Machina focuses on an extremely chaotic band of mercenaries whose competence is considerably less obvious than their capacity for arguing, drinking, and tons of collateral damage.

Industry observers note that the Legend of Vox Machina truly understands the importance of an entertaining ensemble of brilliant characters. The show's critical reception, despite its status as a consistently overlooked gem, has actually been quite exceptional. From its spectacular animation and the show's sharp writing to its combination of crude comedy with elaborate world-building, The Legend of Vox Machina stands as one of the most enjoyable and consistently imaginative watches to emerge over the last five years.

Interview with the Vampire is peak romantic fiction that uses its deeply emotional story and beautiful Gothic atmosphere to thoroughly captivate audiences. The series centers around vampire Louis de Pointe du Lac (Jacob Anderson), who does a second tell-all with veteran journalist Daniel Molloy (Eric Bogosian), diving deep into his beginnings and his eventual destructive relationship with his vampire maker, Lestat de Lioncourt (Sam Reid).

Recent findings suggest that despite Interview with the Vampire being a genuine masterpiece in TV storytelling, the series is still pretty overlooked. The show accomplishes something truly rare: it respects Anne Rice's mythology while radically rethinking sexuality, chronology, race, and historical context in exciting ways that deepen rather than dilute the material. With its exceptional performances, psychological complexity, and distinctive gothic atmosphere, Interview with the Vampire makes for a powerful example of modern fantasy storytelling.

Industry observers note that this anime fantasy is honestly one of the strongest in the genre of the last five years, and it has a lot to do with the series' extraordinary perspective on a very familiar fantasy formula. Set after the hero party has defeated the Demon King, Frieren: Beyond Journey's End follows the elven mage who helped in the battle and is confronted with the passage of time, loss, and the brutal realization of just how fleeting human lives truly are.

Sources indicate that frieren: Beyond Journey's End is a pretty incredible fantasy series—one that has garnered much praise for its captivating story. The show is the absolute perfect watch for how well its fantasy premise is so deeply woven into its emotional storytelling. Frieren: Beyond Journey's End is a remarkable masterpiece with imaginative world-building and emotional depth, which marks it as one of the most perfect fantasy series of the past half-decade.

That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

Sources indicate that the redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final enhancement.

In a recent development, for Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

It has been revealed that for iPhone Duo customers, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Industry observers note that reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

In a recent development, iOS 27.3 also brings a fresh face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

According to recent reports, finally, iOS 27.3 includes a fresh option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with upcoming clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The revision also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

We started rolling out these newly introduced capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

Recent findings suggest that there are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test fresh ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Industry observers note that today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to latest languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

Industry observers note that you can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ proposal, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

iOS 27.3 is a major patch to Safari. First, the update adds support for a newly introduced vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

It has been revealed that iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music people, iOS 27.3 adds a newly introduced “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The enhancement also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Recent findings suggest that second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a new “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Frederick Wiseman’s Complete Filmography to Be Distributed by Janus Films

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you wanted to be a completionist for the movies of documentary legend Frederick Wiseman, or if you have a blind spot for Wiseman’s formalist portraits of American institutions dating back decades, today is your lucky day.
  • Recent findings suggest that janus Films has acquired the North American distribution rights to the complete collection of 45 feature films from Wiseman’s career dating back to his seminal “Titicut Follies” in 1967, and Janus plans to distribute all of them beginning January 1, 2027.
  • Specific distribution plans haven’t been confirmed yet, be it whether these films are going to be seen theatrically, via streaming, or on physical release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you wanted to be a completionist for the movies of documentary legend Frederick Wiseman, or if you have a blind spot for Wiseman’s formalist portraits of American institutions dating back decades, today is your lucky day.

Recent findings suggest that janus Films has acquired the North American distribution rights to the complete collection of 45 feature films from Wiseman’s career dating back to his seminal “Titicut Follies” in 1967, and Janus plans to distribute all of them beginning January 1, 2027. Janus already has a library that includes the works of Agnès Varda, Ingmar Bergman, Akira Kurosawa, Chantal Akerman, and Edward Yang, so Wiseman finds himself in good firm. Related Stories Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56.

Specific distribution plans haven’t been confirmed yet, be it whether these films are going to be seen theatrically, via streaming, or on physical release. But Wiseman’s early films, everything from “Titicut Follies” in 1967 through “State Legislature” in 2007 have been restored in 4K by Wiseman’s Zipporah Films. “La Danse” (2009) through his final feature “Menus-Plaisirs – Les Troisgros” (2023) will be available in their original digital formats.

It has been revealed that this is the first time any distributor other than Zipporah Films is licensing Wiseman’s work in North America, so the hope is that the late documentarian can now reach an even greater audience. It wasn’t until as recently as 2024, that Wiseman’s movies were even all available in digital formats.

Sources indicate that “We couldn’t imagine a better home in North America for Frederick Wiseman’s films than with Janus Films,” said Karen Konicek of Zipporah Films. “It has been an honor to work alongside Fred for so many decades, producing and distributing his films. As Zipporah Films continues as the rights holder and distributor of the Wiseman Collection, we very much look forward to this fresh partnership with Janus Films and are excited to collaborate with them.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We are honored and thrilled to be the first distributor, in the US, outside of Zipporah Films, to be entrusted with licensing one of the greatest bodies of work in American cinema” noted Peter Becker, President of Janus Films and Criterion. “We’re looking forward to presenting these monumental works, theatrically, to new audiences across the country.”.

Wiseman passed away earlier this year in February 2026 at 96 years old. Not only was he one of the most influential documentarians in American cinema, he was one of the most prolific considering the 45 features he independently produced, directed, and edited over his 50-year career.

In 2016, Wiseman received an Honorary Oscar for lifetime achievement from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Board of Governors for his “masterful and distinctive documentaries [that] examine the familiar and reveal the unexpected.”.

IndieWire spoke with Wiseman in 2025 as Lincoln Center prepared a retrospective of all his early films as part of the 4K restoration effort. He spoke about the attention to detail in his editing and his examination of each institution and its layers, despite the enormous length of many of his films.

“The subjects I choose to make films about are complicated, and I think I have an obligation when I’ve been given permission to make a movie about a place to have the final film reflect the complexity of the institution and not just be some superficial, banal representation of the institution,” he mentioned.

The full list of titles acquired by Janus for North American distribution is below:.

“Titicut Follies” (1967), “High School” (1968,) “Law and Order” (1969), “Hospital” (1970), “Basic Training” (1971), “Essene” (1972), “Juvenile Court” (1973), “Primate” (1974), “Welfare” (1975), “Meat” (1976), “Canal Zone” (1977), “Sinai Field Mission” (1978), “Manoeuvre” (1979), “Model” (1980), “The Store” (1983), “Deaf” (1986), “Blind” (1986), “Racetrack” (1985), “Adjustment & Work” (1986), “Multi-handicapped” (1986), “Missile” (1987), “Near Death” (1989), “Central Park” (1990), “Aspen” (1991), “Zoo” (1993), “High School II” (1994), “Ballet” (1995), “La Comédie-Française ou L’amour joué” (1996), “Public Housing” (1997), “Belfast, Maine” (1999), “Domestic Violence” (2001), “Domestic Violence 2” (2002), “The Last Letter” (2002), “State Legislature” (2007), “La Danse: The Paris Opera Ballet” (2009), “Boxing Gym” (2010), “Crazy Horse” (2011), “At Berkeley” (2013), “National Gallery” (2014), “In Jackson Heights” (2015), “Ex Libris: The Upcoming York Public Library” (2017), “Monrovia, Indiana” (2018), “City Hall” (2020), “A Couple” (2022), and “Menus-Plaisirs, les Troisgros” (2023).

Sources indicate that nothing's first over-ear headphones, the Headphone (1), is $130 off for Amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale, bringing them down to $169 from $299 (their lowest price ever). Nothing's newer Headphone (a), which debuted in 2026 and earned an "excellent" rating in PCMag's review, is on sale as well, dropping to $109 from $199. According to recent reports, in line with the manufacturer’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

But the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

Recent findings suggest that that mentioned, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The kitchen tap gets a workout over the holidays. There’s coffee to brew before everyone’s up, a pot of soup on the stove, and a pitcher that always seems to need refilling right as dinner hits the table.

Whether you’re paying closer attention to family health or simply want better-tasting water for coffee and cooking, Waterdrop Filter has options for different kitchens and budgets. Its Black Friday & Cyber Monday deals run November 19 through November 30, with savings of up to $700 on premium RO water filtration and more affordable everyday filters. Use code 9TO5MBF26 for an extra 5% off the five systems featured below, on top of their listed sale prices.

From a Waterdrop reverse osmosis system for a busy family kitchen to a countertop dispenser for a smaller apartment, here’s how to find a home water upgrade that fits your routine.

The best under-sink water filter for your home depends in part on how many people are filling glasses and cooking at once. For families of six or more and frequent hosts, the Waterdrop X16 Alkaline Mineral Reverse Osmosis System is the flagship option.

Sources indicate that its capacity of up to 1,600 gallons per day helps keep water flowing when everyone’s getting ready in the morning or preparing a holiday meal. The 11-stage filtration system adds calcium and magnesium back after reverse osmosis for a more balanced taste, while the tankless design leaves more room beneath the sink.

The smart faucet lets you check filter life at a glance. The X16 is known for its fast dispensing and compact design. During the sale, it’s $1,299, down from $1,999, saving $700, or ~35%.

Industry observers note that for a family of four or five, the Waterdrop G3P800 Reverse Osmosis System brings under-sink reverse osmosis to the kitchen for less. It offers up to 800 gallons per day, with 10-stage filtration, UV sterilization, and a smart faucet that shows filter status.

Both systems have a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio, producing three parts filtered water for each part sent to the drain. Waterdrop notes the X16 and G3P800 help reduce contaminants including lead, PFOA, and PFOS. Waterdrop also lists NSF/ANSI certifications for both models, covering reverse osmosis performance and lead content in the materials. The G3P800 carries additional certifications covering taste-related filtration and specific contaminant-reduction claims.

G3P800 is recognized for its straightforward filter changes and the difference it makes for water, coffee, and tea. It’s $699 during the sale, down from $999, for $300 in savings and 30% off.

If you’re shopping for a reverse osmosis water filter, countertop models make it possible to upgrade without changing the plumbing beneath your sink. Renters, apartment residents, and anyone who wants water ready for tea at the touch of a button may prefer a countertop RO system.

The Waterdrop M6CG Mineral Hot & Cold Reverse Osmosis System combines countertop reverse osmosis, remineralization, and hot and cold dispensing in one appliance. Its 59°F to 203°F temperature range covers everything from a cool glass of water to tea, cocoa, and other hot drinks.

Recent findings suggest that five volume settings and a customizable Favorite Mode let you save your preferred temperature and serving size. There’s also a detachable 40-ounce glass pitcher you can carry straight to the dinner table, which is handy for family meals and holiday hosting. Separate feed-water and wastewater tanks keep the two apart, and the M6CG has the same 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio as the under-sink models.

The M6CG is $409 during the sale, down from $539, saving $130, or ~24%.

For a more affordable countertop water filtration system, the Waterdrop CT01 Instant Hot & Cold Water Filter Dispenser offers the same temperature range with six-stage non-RO filtration. It helps reduce chlorine, rust, and sediment while retaining minerals, and it produces no wastewater.

Like the M6CG, the CT01 requires no installation. Its 1.32-gallon tank means fewer trips to refill it throughout the day, whether you’re keeping water on hand at your desk or making another round of tea. For winter hydration, having hot and cold filtered water ready in one place is a convenient addition to the kitchen.

The CT01 is $199.99 during the Black Friday sale (20% off).

If you mainly want to improve the taste of the water from your existing tap, the Waterdrop TSA 8 Layer Under Sink Water Filter System is an accessible place to start.

In a recent development, it connects to your cold-water line and uses eight-stage filtration to help reduce chlorine, sediment, and other impurities. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are precious few psychological thrillers that can claim to have no bad episodes, but one HBO show from 2018 manages to pull off this feat throughout its unpredictable eight-episode story. From the iconic True Detective season 1 to 2021’s unsparing detective drama Mare of Easttown, HBO has long been home to some of the best psychological thrillers on TV or streaming. In recent years, streaming shows like Netflix’s You and Prime Video’s 56 Days have muscled in on this territory.

In a recent development, however, while those campy hits can be a lot of fun, HBO’s best psychological thrillers come with a level of prestige and artistic credibility that is hard to come by. The cable network has managed quite an impressive feat, turning a genre that can often be seen as trashy or low-rent into acclaimed high art. Much like HBO’s dystopian sci-fi dramas Station Eleven and The Last of Us were lauded as masterpieces despite their sci-fi origins, the network has produced psychological thrillers that transcend the dubious reputation of the genre.

According to recent reports, for many viewers, the phrase “psychological thriller” conjures up iconic, but undeniably lurid movies like Basic Instinct or Fatal Attraction. To be clear, HBO’s eight-episode psychological thriller masterpiece from 2018 is absolutely as creepy, lurid, and itching-ly addictive as those earlier movies, but Sharp Objects is also a taut, enthralling character study that takes potentially hoary southern gothic clichés and makes them feel brutally real.

Set in the fictional small town of Wind Gap, Missouri, Sharp Objects is based on author Gillian Flynn’s claustrophobic debut thriller novel of the same name from 2006. Sharp Objects follows the troubled alcoholic reporter Camille Preaker, played by a career-best Amy Adams, as she returns to the hometown she still hates to reluctantly report on a spate of vicious killings.

It has been revealed that the victims are all teenage girls, as is Camille’s half-sister, Amma. Camille’s memories of Wind Gap are haunted by both her cold, calculating mother and the sister she lost years earlier, but Sharp Objects is by no means a maudlin melodrama.

Instead, Sharp Objects feels as much like HBO’s later horror hits Lovecraft Country or IT: Welcome to Derry as it does Desperate Housewives. Admittedly, the horrors of Sharp Objects are not supernatural in nature, but the show’s oppressively bleak and creepy atmosphere makes the Flynn adaptation a classic piece of Southern Gothic nonetheless.

Sharp Objects wisely opts to ratchet up the tension of its murder mystery story gradually, meaning even the episodes with the least on-screen action are deeply unsettling. As a result, HBO’s Flynn adaptation is a rare psychological thriller with no filler and no padding, as Sharp Objects doesn’t need a constant stream of twists, misdirections, and red herrings to keep viewers occupied.

Instead, Sharp Objects makes it fairly obvious who the villains are early on in the show’s story, and the rest of the series is spent watching a net slowly close in on Camille. Like HBO’s later thriller Lanterns, Sharp Objects takes its time solving the central mystery and merges its dual timelines frequently, but its flashbacks never feel superfluous or excessive. This is superb news for the cable network’s upcoming Flynn series.

Industry observers note that according to Variety, HBO is set to finally follow up Sharp Objects with a belated take on Flynn’s second novel from 2009, Dark Places. A lot of the same creative team will reunite for this series, meaning the show can reasonably hope to avoid the largely negative critical reception of 2015’s misjudged movie adaptation of Dark Places. However, even with a great team behind the camera, any HBO psychological thriller would struggle to replicate the success of Sharp Objects.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erielle Sudario is a Collider News and Feature Author from Australia and has worked in the journalism industry since 2018. She has a passion for entertainment and pop culture news and has interviewed YouTubers, voice actors, film directors, and musicians throughout her career. When she's not writing, you can see Erielle building keyboards, reading a good book, playing video games, and creating content on social media.

It has been revealed that with only a month until Jumanji's fourth and final film, Jumanji: Open World hits theaters, fans will have the chance to immerse themselves in its adventurous world. A brand-new VR experience has been announced, letting players face challenges, bond with exotic animals, and solve puzzles as the "fate of Jumanji" falls into their hands. If you want to know what it's like to be Dr. Bravestone, this would be your chance.

The Jumanji film series began in 1995 and was based on the 1981 children's picture book by Chris Van Allsburg. The movie stars Robin Williams, Kirsten Dunst, David Alan Grier, and Bonnie Hunt, and the story follows two kids who play a magic board game whose effects spill into real life, like animals and hunters appearing in their world. In 2017, the board game returned, this time transformed into a video game, where a fresh generation of players were sucked in and had to complete it to get home.

Sources indicate that now, free-roam VR entertainment organization Zero Latency has announced a brand-upcoming game coming out this December called Jumanji: The Lost Levels. According to a press release, the company worked closely with Sony Pictures to create an original story that ensures that it "captures the wild, funny and chaotic Jumanji energy." This is what the game's description has to say:.

"Players will navigate the perils of Jumanji across a series of escalating challenges: forge bonds with exotic animal companions, survive an exhilarating river rafting gauntlet, bust out their best moves in a snake dance-off (yes, really), crack the secrets of ancient temple puzzles, saddle up and ride dinosaurs through uncharted jungle, and face off against an epic boss battle with the fate of Jumanji itself hanging in the balance.".

The trailer for the upcoming game shows players controlling the same avatars seen in the movie as they explore the jungle and dangerous locations that thrust them straight into the adventure. Zero Latency first started in 2013, and since then, it has expanded worldwide, with over 30 locations in the U.S. alone, with six more venues opening soon.

It has been revealed that jumanji: Open World is the fifth installment and final entry in the Jumanji franchise. The movie takes place immediately after the events of Jumanji: The Next Level, as the world of Jumanji breaks free from its video game console and enters the real world. The video game avatars of Dr. Smolder Bravestone (Dwayne Johnson), Professor Sheldon Oberon (Jack Black), Franklin Finbar (Kevin Hart), and Ruby Roundhouse (Karen Gillan) roam the real world in "demo mode." It's now up to Spencer Gilpin (Alex Wolff) to set things right, and joining him in the game are his mother, Janice (Marin Hinkle), kitchen worker Donatas (Dan Hildebrand), and Tyson Shepherd (Jack Jewkes).

Jumanji: Open World will enter theaters on December 25, 2026, while Zero Latency's Jumanji: The Lost Levels will be released worldwide on December 4, 2026. Follow Collider for more updates.

Amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale has brought the Sonos Arc Ultra down to $849 from its usual $1,099, a $250 discount that marks its lowest price yet. PCMag named it the best soundbar of 2024 and gave it an “outstanding” rating in its review. Still, $849 is a lot to spend on a single soundbar, and anyone shopping on a tighter budget will find more affordable picks in our Fire TV soundbar roundup. For more editor-vetted tech deals, check out our comprehensive Black Friday coverage.

For those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to proposal around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. Despite all that width, it keeps a low profile at just under three inches tall, so it can sit beneath most screens without blocking the picture, or you can wall-mount it if you would rather keep your TV stand clear. All that size makes room for a 9.1.4-channel layout (a substantial step up from the original Arc) that gives Dolby Atmos effects more space to spread around and above you. Sonos also added a new Sound Motion driver that it claims doubles the original Arc's bass, giving action scenes real weight without a separate subwoofer, though you can still add a Sub 4 later for more rumble.

At the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far
